questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution mentions oath or affirmation by the Governor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 159**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The oath or affirmation to be taken by the Governor is mentioned in **Article 159** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This article outlines the procedure for the appointment of the Governor and the oath that he or she must take upon assuming office.
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Governor holds office for a term of five years but can be removed from office by the President if he or she resigns,
 
 
• is impeached by the state legislature, or is removed by the President on the advice of the Union Cabinet.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Article 156: Governor's Term of Office
 
 
• The Governor holds office for a term of five years from the date he or she enters upon his or her office.
 
• The Governor can be removed from office by the President of India:
 
• If he or she resigns.
 
• If he or she is impeached by the state legislature.
 
• If he or she is removed by the President on the advice of the Union Cabinet.
 
 
 
• Article 161: Governor's Powers
 
 
• The Governor exercises executive powers in the state.
 
• This includes:
 
 
• Appointing and removing ministers.
 
• Issuing ordinances.
 
• Granting pardons, reprieves, and remissions of punishment.

questions.question: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 granted the British colonial government the power to arrest and detains Indians without trial. Who was the British Viceroy of India at that time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is. __Lord Chelmsford__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The Rowlatt Act was passed by the government under the period of Lord Chelmsford.
 
• **It was passed in February 1919.**
 
• Every single Indian member of the Central Legislative Council opposed it.
 
• The** act authorised the government to imprison any suspect without trial** and conviction in the court of law.
 
• It enables the government to suppress the habeas corpus.
 
• They wanted to replace the provision of repression during wartime Defence of India Act 1915 by a permanent law.
 
• **It was based on the report of Justice S.A.T. Rowlatt’s Committee of 1918.**
 
• The act was resented by the Indian public and opposed by all Indian members of the Council.
 
• **Gandhi organised a protest movement which led to the Massacre of Amritsar (April 1919).**
 
• The act was never actually implemented.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Curzon (Viceroy of India: 1899–1905)**

 
 
• Lord Curzon is **known for implementing several administrative reforms in India, including the division of Bengal in 1905, **which led to widespread protests and was later reversed after his tenure.
 
• He** prioritized infrastructure developmen**t, notably the expansion of railways and improvements in the telecommunication system.
 
• Curzon made significant contributions to the preservation of India's cultural heritage, **including the establishment of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI**) and the restoration of several historical sites.
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie (Governor-General of India: 1848–1856)**
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie is most famous for the implementation of the Doctrine of Lapse**, which led to the annexation of several Indian states when rulers died without a male heir.
 
• He is **credited with the introduction of railways in India,** which played a major role in the economic and logistical development of the country.
 
• Dalhousie **supported the development of Western education** in India, including the foundation of universities in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.
 
 
 
• **Lord Irwin (Viceroy of India: 1926–1931)**
 
 
• **Lord Irwin’s tenure saw the appointment of the Simon Commission in 1927,** which was boycotted by Indian leaders as it did not include any Indian members.
 
• His **policies contributed to the rise of Mahatma Gandhi's Civil Disobedience Movement, notably the Salt March in 1930**, which was a direct challenge to British colonial rule.
 
• **Lord Irwin was involved in discussions that led to the Government of India Act 1935**, which expanded the participation of Indians in governance, though it was seen as insufficient by many.

questions.question: The Palaeolithic period extends from 2 million years ago to about 12,000 years ago. This long stretch of time is divided into the Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic. This long span of time covers ________ percent of human history.

• This long span of time covers 99% of human history
 
• Archaeologists have given lengthy names for the time that we are studying.
 
• They call the earliest period the Palaeolithic. This comes from two Greek words, ‘palaeo’, meaning old, and ‘lithos’, meaning stone.
 
• The name points to the importance of finds of stone tools.
 
• The Palaeolithic period extends from 2 million years ago to about 12,000 years ago.
 
• This long stretch of time is divided into the Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic.
 
• The Palaeolithic cultures flourished in the geological era called the Pleistocene.
 
• In this period Homo erectus first time used fire, made stone tools and other implements, 
 
 
• and used the clean skin of other animals therefore may be taken to represent the beginning of true man. 
 
 
 
• The Pleistocene era, climatically, is characterised by glacial (extreme cold conditions and extensive ice caps) and interglacial (warm period) conditions in the temperate zones and pluvial (heavy rainy or wet period) and interpluvial (dry period) conditions in the tropical belt.
 
• Early human populations (i.e. Palaeolithic) lived in major parts of the temperate zones (Europe) and tropical zones (Africa and Asia) successfully adapting to these climatic events and environments.
 
• Evidence of fire in the form of a hearth is known from Upper Palaeolithic caves in the Kurnool area and is dated to about 16,000 years ago.

questions.question:
Read the following about Liabilities.

A. Liabilities for any firm are its debts or what it owes to others.

B. For a bank, the main liability is the deposits which people keep with it.

Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Liabilities represent the debts or financial obligations that a firm owes to external parties.
 
• For a bank, the main liability is the **deposits held by customers**, which are funds that the bank must repay on demand or at the end of an agreed term.
 
• These liabilities include **current accounts, savings accounts, and fixed deposits**, each with varying levels of withdrawal flexibility and interest terms.
 
• In a bank's balance sheet, deposits are listed as liabilities since the bank is obligated to return them to the depositors.
 
• Deposits form the foundation of a bank’s lending operations, as the bank uses these liabilities to create assets in the form of loans and investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Bank Deposits:**

 
 
• **Current Accounts:** Used for frequent transactions, no interest is typically paid.
 
• **Savings Accounts**: Offer interest on the deposited amount but with some limitations on withdrawals.
 
• **Fixed Deposits**: Customers deposit money for a fixed term, earning a higher interest rate.
 
 
 
• **Balance Sheet Representation:** In a bank’s balance sheet, deposits are shown under the liabilities section since they represent an obligation for the bank to repay.
 
• **Banking Operations:** Deposits are crucial as they provide the bank with the funds necessary to extend loans. This lending activity, in turn, generates income for the bank through interest on loans.
 
• **Liquidity Management:** Banks need to manage their liabilities carefully to ensure they can meet deposit withdrawals when required, maintaining sufficient liquidity.
 
• **Interest Payments: **Deposits are classified as interest-bearing liabilities because the bank is required to pay interest on savings and fixed deposits.
 
• **Risk of Liabilities:** The NCERT books emphasize that a bank's ability to manage its liabilities, particularly customer deposits, directly affects its financial health and stability.

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 60 percent more than its cost price. If the article is sold for Rs. 300 after offering a discount of Rs. 20, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) is 60% more than Cost Price (CP).

Selling Price (SP) = ₹300

Discount = ₹20

**Calculations:**

1. Calculate the Marked Price (MP):

⇒ SP = MP - Discount

⇒ 300 = MP - 20

⇒ MP = 300 + 20 = 320

2. Establish the relationship between CP and MP:

⇒ MP = CP + (60/100) × CP

⇒ MP = CP × (1 + 0.6)

⇒ MP = CP × 1.6

3. Calculate CP from MP:

⇒ 320 = CP × 1.6

⇒ CP = 320 / 1.6

⇒ CP = 200

4. Calculate Profit:

⇒ Profit = SP - CP

⇒ Profit = 300 - 200 = 100

5. Calculate Profit Percentage:

⇒ Profit Percentage = (Profit / CP) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = (100 / 200) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 50%

**∴ The profit percentage is 50%.**

questions.question: If a certain sum of money becomes thrice of itself in 7 years 3 months at simple interest, then what will be the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Amount becomes thrice in 7 years 3 months.

Time (T) = 7 years + 3 months = 7 + 0.25 = 7.25 years.

Let the principal amount be P. The total amount after 7.25 years will be 3P.

Using the formula for Simple Interest: A = P + SI, where SI = P × R × T / 100.

So, 3P = P + (P × R × 7.25 / 100).

Rearranging gives: 3P - P = P × R × 7.25 / 100.

Thus, 2P = P × R × 7.25 / 100.

Dividing both sides by P (assuming P ≠ 0): 2 = R × 7.25 / 100.

Multiplying both sides by 100: 200 = R × 7.25.

Finally, R = 200 / 7.25 ≈ 27.59%.

**The annual rate of interest is approximately 27.59%.**
